newsitem.title: USA: Wis. ballpark district can live with amended bill.
newsitem.headline: Wis. ballpark district can live with amended bill.

text.p: A member of the board overseeing the financing and construction of the new ballpark for the Milwaukee Brewers American League baseball team said Wednesday he finds a state legislative compromise bill limiting the powers of the district to be "livable."

The Wisconsin Senate's judiciary committee earlier Wednesday passed a bill imposing limits on the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District, but reducing restrictions contained in an earlier version, according to a committee clerk.
The compromise between the committee chairman, Sen. Lynn Adelman, D-New Berlin, and the sponsor, Sen. Joe Wineke, D-Verona, was first presented to representatives of the district earlier Wednesday.
As presented, the bill is "livable," said state Rep. Michael Lehman, R-Hartford, who is also a member of the baseball board.

"Removing the state's moral obligation was realistic since we had insured the bonding already," Lehman said, noting that the district had sold $146.7 million of tax-exempt sales tax revenue bonds backed by a five-county sales tax in March that are insured by MBIA Insurance Corp.

The quarterly reports are also something the board already does in general terms, Lehman said. Guaranteeing that the five-county sales tax will end was also something the board could support, he added.
"The original one limited us in potentially completing the facility," Lehman said.
